import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

I've read the first of the four reports (cdx). Now reading the other three. I'm checking bob-cli's code against the reports' claims. Next: how the research-report hook calls `bob ref create`, and what it does when the command fails. The collect pass works: 26 ms on pandoc 3.1.11.1, and its sha1 keys match the rendered diagram files. Writing the consolidated report now. Registered the consolidated report (`file:explicit:061b54e021198c522c8f4cf0`). Cleaning up my scratch files, then finalizing. I read your note as "does **not** convert Mermaid well". The screenshot shows `flowchart LR` printed as wrapped source with literal `
`. It's a missing feature, not a bug: pandoc treats the Mermaid fence as an ordinary code block, and nothing in bob handles it. **Is it a good idea?** Yes, and all four researchers agree. Mermaid in agent-written reports is meant to be a picture, since GitHub and Obsidian render it. Printed as source it wastes pages and can't usefully be highlighted. Nearly all the demand is research reports: about 139 fences across 91 files in the sase research repo, about 44 in this one, and none in the vault. Every one of those reports goes through the unattended `research-highlights` hook that runs `bob ref create`. **Recommended solution:** - **Renderer:** vendor a pinned copy of Mermaid 12.x into bob and run it inside the Playwright/Chrome adapter that web capture already uses. One offline browser launch handles every diagram in a document. - **Output:** each diagram becomes a tightly cropped vector PDF, so its labels stay real, selectable text. - **Wiring:** a cheap Rust scan skips documents with no Mermaid. A quick pandoc pass (26 ms) finds the exact diagram blocks. A small Lua filter, run first in both Markdown routes, swaps each block for its PDF. pandoc and XeLaTeX are otherwise unchanged. - **Failures:** a bad diagram keeps its source under a visible note ("Mermaid diagram not rendered: …") plus a warning, and the import still succeeds. **Where the researchers disagreed:** - **`mmdc` (Mermaid's command-line tool):** rejected. - It isn't installed on the Mac, and its current version needs Node 22.13 or newer. - On athena it failed out of the box twice: a missing bundled Chrome, then a "socket path too long" crash. - It starts Chrome once per diagram, about 24 s for the 12-diagram report in your screenshot versus about 2–3 s per document with the adapter. - **`mmdr` (a Rust reimplementation of Mermaid):** rejected. I built version 0.3.1 and rendered your screenshot's diagram. It placed the two chains side by side, 2491 px wide against 1196 px from real Mermaid, which would print labels at about 3 pt. - **PNG output:** rejected because it loses selectable text. - **Aborting on a bad diagram:** rejected. One agent's typo shouldn't drop a whole 17-page report from the unattended hook. **Adjustments to your requirements:** - **Scope:** render only explicitly tagged Mermaid blocks, in both regular Markdown files and vault-note snapshots (including `-M`). Never guess at untagged code blocks. - **Failure:** fall back visibly per diagram; never abort the import and never hide the fallback. - **Font:** diagrams must use a static TTF font. Earlier Highlights testing found 5.4% damaged quotes with the font type Chrome produces from variable fonts. My test of a bundled DejaVu Sans font, loaded with all network requests blocked, embedded cleanly. - **Look:** turn off the theme's CSS effects. Mermaid 12.2.0's drop shadows otherwise get rasterized into 12–18 small images per diagram. With them off, the flowchart PDF shrank from 87 KB to 16 KB with no raster images. - **Pinning:** use the vendored copy only; never a host install or online service, and no network during rendering. - **No new CLI flag:** every long option would need a short alias. An env variable can switch the feature off instead. Dry-run never starts a browser, and doctor only warns. - **Wide diagrams:** they scale down rather than being rewritten. Your screenshot's chart lands at about 6.5 pt labels; warn below roughly half scale and leave landscape pages for later. - **No backfill:** don't re-render existing library PDFs, since your highlights live in them. - **Different approach:** a cheap complement is nudging the research-report prompts toward top-down flowcharts with short labels. **Still unverified:** nobody has checked on the Mac that you can select and highlight text inside an embedded diagram in Highlights. It's an acceptance item in the report. The consolidated report is `202610/ref_create_mermaid_figures/ref_create_mermaid_figures__final.md` in the research repo. My test scripts and comparison images are in the `ref_create_mermaid_figures__final_assets/` folder beside it. The four reports moved into that directory under the new name, along with grk's evidence images. The report is registered for the linker as `research:202610/ref_create_mermaid_figures/ref_create_mermaid_figures__final.md` (`file:explicit:061b54e021198c522c8f4cf0`). The research repo commit is declared and will be made when this turn ends.
